CHIEF COMPLAINT
Suspected kidney stone with left-sided back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents with left-sided back pain that began three days ago. Pain is constant in nature and has been radiating lower toward the groin area. Patient reports she has not yet passed the stone. Patient is able to urinate and noted blood in urine this morning. This is the patient's third episode of kidney stones. She reports previous episodes have typically resolved within three to four days. Patient has taken Tylenol and ibuprofen with minimal relief. Patient reports severe pain preventing her from eating.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies fever. Reports some chills and mild nausea. Denies chest pain and abdominal pain, though notes pain extending into groin area. Reports hematuria.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes mellitus
History of kidney stones (third episode)
Systolic ejection murmur (grade 2/6)

MEDICATIONS
Norvasc 2.5 mg for hypertension
Metformin 500 mg for diabetes
Tylenol as needed for pain
Ibuprofen as needed for pain

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports enjoying high-salt foods such as french fries and acknowledges difficulty with dietary adherence.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Heart: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur noted
Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles or wheezes
Abdomen: Tender to palpation, no rebound or guarding
Costovertebral angle: Tenderness on right flank

RESULTS
Fasting blood glucose: Low 100s (recent readings)
A1C: 7.3
Blood glucose on prior visit (approximately 2 months ago): 300
Home blood pressure readings: Systolic 130-150, diastolic 70-80

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Kidney stone: Diagnosed based on clinical presentation and physical examination findings. Prescribed oxycodone 5 mg every 6 to 8 hours as needed for pain management. Advised to continue Tylenol for breakthrough pain. Instructed to increase fluid intake to promote stone passage. Provided urine strainer. Referred to urology for evaluation given recurrent kidney stone episodes.

Hypertension: Continue Norvasc 2.5 mg. Blood pressure control currently adequate. Encouraged to continue home blood pressure monitoring at least three times weekly. Discussed sodium restriction to 2300 mg daily.

Diabetes mellitus: Continue Metformin 500 mg daily. Recent fasting glucose levels improved. Referred to nutrition/dietitian for dietary counseling.
